item.title: Keeping critical infrastructure safe with EN ISO 24817:2026
item.description: Pressurized systems are found at the core of many of our key industries, including hospitals, chemical plants, and nuclear power stations – they are even in the heating systems in our homes. Sudden failure of these systems can be catastrophic, so industry first started work to standardize the design, operation, and maintenance in the 1880s. EN ISO 24817:2026 provides guidance on using advanced composite materials such as carbon or glass fibre reinforced epoxy resins (as an alternative to traditional methods) to enable the continued, safe operation of pressurized systems where inspection identifies points of concern. item.title: "Standards are a backbone of the Single Market": CEN and CENELEC contribute to IMCO hearing on the European Product Act
item.description: On 15 October, Andreea Gulacsi, Director of Policy and External Affairs at CEN and CENELEC, participated in a public hearing of the European Parliament's Committee on the Internal Market and Consumer Protection (IMCO) on the European Product Act. The hearing brought together representatives of the European Commission, national authorities, consumer organizations, industry and standardization bodies to discuss the New Standardization Regulation as well as the upcoming European Product Act that will set the future of EU product legislation. Speaking during the hearing's second panel, Andreea Gulacsi underlined the essential role of standards in supporting Europe's Single Market and highlighted the need for a strong public-private partnership in standardization. item.title: First ever European standard on AI published in the OJEU
item.description: World Standards Day this year marked an additional milestone for Europe's AI ecosystem. The day coincided with the publication in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJEU) of the Commission Implementing Decision citing the first harmonized standard in support of the AI Act: EN 18286:2026 'Artificial Intelligence – Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes'. As the first harmonized standard in support of the AI Act, EN 18286:2026 is a landmark achievement for the European AI ecosystem. It bridges the gap between regulation and implementation by translating the quality management system requirements of Article 17 into practical, auditable requirements that providers of high-risk AI systems can readily apply. item.title: Draft CWA for comment: Mathematical Simulation models for real time, SIMBOTs
item.description: Data centres and server rooms are increasingly important in our digitised world. But such areas require an advanced upkeep and use a great amount of energy. Support for our IT infrastructures in an efficient and intelligent manner – digital and physical – is a necessity. For the past three years, the Hybrid COOLing & management for IT project has been focussing its energies on the smart management of electricity consumption of server rooms in tertiary buildings. Its key goal is to develop a set of processes that can be replicated through standardization. item.title: Launch of the CEN Workshop 'UNITED CIRCLES - Feasibility to Finance Guidelines for Industrial-Urban Symbiosis within Hubs for Circularity'
item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being established to develop a CEN Workshop Agreement (CWA) entitled 'Feasibility to Finance Guidelines for Industrial-Urban Symbiosis within Hubs for Circularity: the UNITED CIRCLES Approach'. The Workshop stems from work being done in UNITED CIRCLES Horizon project aiming to provide practical guidance for advancing Industrial-Urban Symbiosis (IUS) from feasibility assessment to investment readiness. Industrial-Urban Symbiosis is increasingly recognized as a key enabler of the circular economy, supporting the recovery and valorisation of materials, energy, water and other resources through collaboration between industries, cities and local stakeholders. item.title: Europe’s competitiveness needs a stronger standardization system – not a fragmented one
item.description: Today, the European Commission published its proposal for the New Standardization Regulation, which would repeal Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012. CEN and CENELEC support the objective of making European standardization faster and more effective. However, several elements of the proposal risk weakening the very system it seeks to improve. Reform should strengthen, not fragment, the successful system Europe already has. For decades, this independent, consensus-based public-private partnership has brought together industry, SMEs, public authorities, consumers, researchers and societal stakeholders through national participation.
